verses.text: Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a spring of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! For they are all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.
“They bend their tongue, as their bow, for falsehood; and they have grown strong in the land, but not for truth: for they proceed from evil to evil, and they don’t know me,” says Yahweh.
“Everyone beware of his neighbor, and don’t trust in any brother; for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbor will go about with slanders.
Everyone will deceive their neighbors, and will not speak the truth. They have taught their tongue to speak lies. They weary themselves commiting iniquity.
Your habitation is in the middle of deceit; through deceit they refuse to know me,” says Yahweh.
Therefore Yahweh of Armies says, “Behold, I will melt them, and try them; for how should I deal with the daughter of my people?
Their tongue is a deadly arrow. It speaks deceit. One speaks peaceably to his neighbor with his mouth, but in his heart, he lays wait for him.
Shall I not punish them for these things?” says Yahweh. “Shouldn’t my soul be avenged on a nation such as this?

I will weep and wail for the mountains, and lament for the pastures of the wilderness, because they are burned up, so that no one passes through; neither can men hear the voice of the livestock. Both the birds of the sky and the animals have fled. They are gone.
“I will make Jerusalem heaps, a dwelling place of jackals. I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.”

Who is wise enough to understand this? Who is he to whom the mouth of Yahweh has spoken, that he may declare it? Why is the land perished and burned up like a wilderness, so that no one passes through?
Yahweh says, “Because they have forsaken my law which I set before them, and have not obeyed my voice, neither walked therein,
but have walked after the stubbornness of their own heart, and after the Baals, which their fathers taught them.”
therefore Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says, “Behold, I will feed them, even this people, with wormwood, and give them water of gall to drink.
I will scatter them also among the nations, whom neither they nor their fathers have known; and I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them.”
Yahweh of Armies says, “Consider, and call for the mourning women, that they may come; and send for the skillful women, that they may come.
Let them make haste, and take up a wailing for us, that our eyes may run down with tears, and our eyelids gush out with waters.
For a voice of wailing is heard out of Zion, ‘How are we ruined! We are greatly confounded, because we have forsaken the land, because they have cast down our dwellings.’”
Yet hear Yahweh’s word, you women, and let your ear receive the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters wailing, and everyone her neighbor lamentation.
For death has come up into our windows. It has entered into our palaces; to cut off the children from outside, and the young men from the streets.
Speak, “Yahweh says, “‘The dead bodies of men will fall as dung on the open field, and as the handful after the harvester; and no one will gather them.’”
Yahweh says, “Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might. Don’t let the rich man glory in his riches.

But let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight,” says Yahweh.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will punish all those who are circumcised only in their flesh:

Egypt, and Judah, and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab, and all that have the corners of their hair cut off, who dwell in the wilderness; for all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.”

footnotes.content: Jeremiah's heart breaks at the sight of his people's ruin—he wishes he could weep without ceasing. A prophet who loves his nation enough to grieve it. We see Jesus wept over Jerusalem much the same way, moved by what He saw coming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet is exhausted by the betrayal around him—adulterers and treacherous men—and dreams of escape. But the Lord won't let him go. Sometimes loving people means staying in the mess rather than fleeing it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They've bent their tongues like bows, launching arrows of falsehood. The Lord sees it plainly: they don't know Him. Sin isn't just bad behavior—it's a broken relationship with the One who made us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Beware of your neighbor"—trust has collapsed in the land. When a people turn from God, they turn from one another too. Deceit spreads like disease through every household and street.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They've trained their tongues in lies the way a warrior trains for war. And it wearies them—sin exhaust the soul. All that effort to deceive, and for what? The house built on lies always falls.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They dwell in deceit the way others dwell in a city—it's their home, their air, their constant companion. And through it all, they refuse to know the Lord. That refusal is the root of everything that follows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will melt and test His people like ore in fire. Not in cruelty, but because He loves them enough to purify. Judgment is His strange work, but it flows from a Father's heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The tongue is a deadly arrow, sharp and hidden. They greet their neighbor with peace on their lips while planning ambush in their hearts. How often our words betray what we truly are.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord asks: Shall I not punish these things? His question isn't cruel—it's the voice of justice stirred. A nation that abandons truth and trust cannot stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet weeps over the land itself—mountains stripped, pastures burned, no travelers, no animal voices. Creation itself mourns when a people abandon their God. Even the earth groans.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem will become heaps, Judah's cities desolate. The threat is not empty. The Lord speaks what He will do. But even this word carries a hope: if they turn, He will turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Who is wise enough to understand? The prophet poses a puzzle: Why does the land perish? The answer, he'll say, is simple—they've forsaken God's law. Wisdom always circles back to obedience.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God makes it plain: they've abandoned His law and haven't listened to His voice. The relationship was there—set before them—but they chose the other road.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Instead, they've followed their own stubborn hearts and the Baals their fathers taught them. Sin runs in families, but so does grace. One generation can break the chain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will feed them wormwood and give them gall to drink—bitterness for bitterness. Justice tastes like poison to those who've feasted on lies. Yet even this bitter cup can awaken a wanderer home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Scattering among nations they've never known, pursued by the sword—dispersion was the ancient terror. To lose your land, your people, your name. Yet the Lord's hand, even in judgment, remained on them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mourning women were a real custom in ancient Judah—skilled in lamentation, they'd sing dirges for the dead. Here, they're summoned for a nation's death. The Lord speaks of His people's end in terms of ritual loss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let them wail and teach their daughters to wail. Grief must be voiced. To mourn is to acknowledge what's been lost and to honor it. Sometimes nations need to weep before they can heal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zion echoes with the cry: How are we ruined? We've forsaken the land and lost our homes. The voice of loss speaks—and someone must hear it. Acknowledgment is the first step toward return.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yet hear the Lord's word, women. He doesn't stop speaking even in judgment. Teach your daughters lamentation—teach them to feel, to grieve, to know that something precious has been lost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Death has climbed through the windows—invasion has come to the homes and palaces. No place is safe. Children and young men are cut down. The siege is thorough, the cost complete.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The dead lie like dung in the field, unburied, unclaimed—the deepest dishonor in that world. A people forgotten. Yet the Lord sees even the forgotten. He counts them. He grieves them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Let no one glory in wisdom, power, or wealth. These are the pillars people lean on when they turn from God. And each one crumbles in the end.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Only let the one who glories glory in this: knowing the Lord—that He practices loving-kindness, justice, and righteousness. Readers today hear an echo of the same truth: all other glories fade, but the knowledge of God endures. He is still the same God who delights in these three.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord will punish those circumcised only in flesh—the outward sign without the inward heart. Ritual means nothing when the soul is far away. God looks for what's real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab—all nations, circumcised in flesh or not, are uncircumcised in heart. The Lord's judgment falls on the same standard: Does your heart know Him? All humanity stands on level ground before this question.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
